      "observations": [
        "Enables ews account enumeration and native type conversion, adds both manifest-version schema choices and an EWS-specific fake-server test suite. This is preliminary account/folder exposure; it does not claim every folder/message operation is supported.",
        "The fixture configures credentials/ews_url, triggers initial sync and waits for the last fake folder. The last-folder ordering assumption is explicit in the helper comment and is not independent verification of every folder or live Exchange behavior. Cleanup closes cached connections. EWSServer.addMessages is still a TODO.",
        "The new test passes {strict:true} as the third argument to custom assertDeepEqual, but its actual third parameter is description and strict comes from the fourth parameter. Thus the object is not an expected-behavior message and it does not enable strict object-key checking. Shared helper and both call sites were inspected. Current getMailAccounts JSDoc still says it excludes EWS, while its filter excludes only im; code and schema control the observed behavior.",
        "Complete Bug1967386 description/comments0–3 and D252640 full preliminary-support summary/timeline, seven submitted inline bodies and footer read. The reporter asks for full EWS support after list/get/onCreated exclude it, but the author explicitly limits this patch to preliminary account/folder exposure with unsupported operations. Final FIXED status does not expand that capability claim.",
        "The early review reports mock-server Unexpected EWS operation/create-folder failures, then attributes fixes to D252678/D252705. Those linked source bodies and job results were not audited here. Reviewers explain initial sync is needed for hierarchy, well-known folders and the root server-side ID; the author moves this into createAccount, producing an EWS-only Promise in this first patch. A shared cross-directory sync module is postponed. Actual helper waits for the last configured fake folder under an explicit ordering assumption, not a proof against live Exchange.",
        "The actual test manifest loads head.js then head-ews.js and runs one EWS account test; the EWS wrapper supplies the default protocol and forwards the result. Cleanup closes EWS cached connections. Source enumeration includes ews and excludes im despite a stale getMailAccounts JSDoc sentence. Both manifest-version schemas accept ews. These are source facts distinct from supporting every operation.",
        "The new account-shape assertions pass {strict:true} as argument3. The actual custom helper uses argument3 as description and reads strict from argument4, so those calls neither enable strict object-key checking nor provide a useful expected-behavior message. This is retained as a concrete test-contract deficiency; no test or helper was repaired or run. Existing focused account-exposure/fixture lesson is reused."
      ],
